My starting routine
The same 4 steps for every question
READ
Read the rule and the domain written after it.
TEST
Try two inputs, including a pair with opposite signs.
SKETCH
Sketch the graph. Draw a horizontal and a vertical line.
NAME
One-one, many-one or one-many? Check with your table.

The domain can change the answer.
QuestionWatch forExample
Q 2Try inputs with opposite signs.Compare x = 2 and x = −2.
Q 3Odd powers do not behave like x2.Test −2 and 2 in x3 before you decide.
Q 5, Q 7Read the domain before you test.x = −3 is not allowed when x > 0.

a) one-one

Before you open a hint, write your plan in one line:
Hint 1 · Echo
Say it in your own words: “|x| is the distance of x from 0, so it is never negative.”
Hint 2 · Translator
Make a table for x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 and write each output.
Hint 3 · Starter
Begin with one pair of inputs with opposite signs, such as 3 and −3.
YOUR TURN
Look at your table. Do two inputs share an output? Pick the word.
Use the hints one at a time. Try on your own before you read the next one.
Before you start
Read Section 1.1 of the coursebook: the mapping diagram and the table of one-one, many-one and one-many graphs. Keep graph paper ready.
Challenge ahead
Q 8 maps one input to two outputs. Keep it in mind for Section 1.2: can such a mapping be a function?
